decisions.decision: Use one user-facing Flow object across discovery, save, execution and export.
Lead with title, verified source, representative items, required input and result; do not invent popularity proof.
Show the complete artifact before one start-or-adjust decision.
Confirm the save with truthful counts and expose the complete effective Flow in the same decision frame.
Separate cross-Flow now work, saved Flow inventory and completed history while preserving whole-Flow reading.
Keep quick value edits, advanced schedule edits, structural changes and batch movement as distinct modes.
Use Calendar for dated placement, explicit Flow scope and an on-demand undated inbox; preserve one occurrence per executable control.
Expose scope and predicted count before format, then report the actual generated result.
Preserve source, personal overlay, run, occurrence, Calendar event and export identities as separate owners.
Use the local content-usage preview only for minimal-input, source-rail, compact-row and destination-preview comparison.
Do not recruit or claim observed-user validation from automated simulation; observed session count remains zero.
